title.en: The Case of the Fifth Word (a detective story)

text.en: Encyclopedia Brown is a young boy in Idaville, USA, whose father is the Chief of Police. He solves mysteries that even the police cannot.

Encyclopedia Brown lives in Idaville and helps his father, the Chief of Police, solve tough cases.
His friends say he is like a library and a computer rolled into one because he never forgets a fact.
The cases are usually discussed at the dinner table, so the story begins at a Tuesday dinner.
A detective story has a puzzle, clues, suspects and a solution at the end.
The key to solving a mystery is to notice small details and ask whether each statement could be true.
The title warns that a single word, the fifth word, holds the key to the case.
The word case has several meanings: a situation, a legal matter, a container, and a type of letter, such as capital letters.
Matching meanings of case with sentences, like 'the lawyer waited for the case' and 'my pencil case', is the practice in the book.
Mystery stories train us to read carefully and to think logically.
Read the story again and look for the clue before the detective reveals it.

text.en: A legal matter: the lawyer took up the case.
A situation: this is not the case.
